title: nf-core/macproqc pipeline parameters
description: A workflow for the quality control of mass spectrometry-based proteomics analyses

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to comma-separated file containing information about the samples in the experiment.
input.help_text: You will need to create a design file with information about the samples in your experiment before running the pipeline. Use this parameter to specify its location. It has to be a comma-separated file with 3 columns, and a header row. See [usage docs](https://mpc-bioinformatics.github.io/McQuaC/usage/#samplesheet-input).

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

fasta_parameters.title: FASTA parameters
fasta_parameters.description: Database settings, to specify the FASTA, create decoys, ...

fasta.help_text: Path to a single protein database file applied to all MS runs. Whether the file already contains decoys is controlled by --skip_decoy_generation.

skip_decoy_generation.description: Add this parameter when you want to skip the generation of the decoy database.
skip_decoy_generation.help_text: If you want to use your own decoys, you can specify a dataset that includes decoy sequences.

decoy_string.description: String that is combined with the accession of the protein identifier to indicate a decoy protein.
decoy_string.help_text: This is passed to the decoy generation as well as to tools using this. Usually, this is a prefix of the protein accession.

decoy_method.description: Method used to generate decoy sequences.
decoy_method.help_text: Passed directly to OpenMS DecoyDatabase. Valid values are 'reverse' (default) and 'shuffle'. Has no effect when --skip_decoy_generation is set.

save_decoy_database.description: Set this parameter to true to save the generated decoy database (for later usage).

identification_parameters.title: Identification parameters
identification_parameters.description: Search engine specific settings and general settings for the identification of peptides and proteins in MS data. Additional untypical parameters can be adjucted by the modules.config, see there for reference.

comet_config_template.description: This is the default comet parameters file. In this file, parameters can be set, which are neither passed by common runtime (threads, fasta, ...) or by common search engine parameters. If not set or null, the provided default in assets is used.

peptide_mass_tolerance_upper.description: Comet parameter: peptide_mass_tolerance_upper, upper bound of the precursor mass tolerance

peptide_mass_tolerance_lower.description: Comet parameter: peptide_mass_tolerance_lower, lower bound of the precursor mass tolerance; USUALLY NEGATIVE TO BE LOWER THAN 0

fragment_bin_tol.description: Comet parameter: fragment_bin_tol, binning to use on fragment ions

fragment_bin_offset.description: Comet parameter: fragment_bin_offset, offset position to start the binning (0.0 to 1.0)

theoretical_fragment_ions.description: Comet parameter: theoretical_fragment_ions, 0=use flanking peaks, 1=M peak only

psms_per_spectrum.description: Comet parameter: num_output_lines: num peptide results to show

variable_modifications.description: Comet parameter: adjust or add the variable modifications to overwrite in the template. The actual string MUST be in single quotes inside a string, like "'variable_mod01 = 15.9949 M 0 3 -1 0 0 0.0'". Variables are defined like in the comet params file (with 'variable_modXX = ...'). Multiple modifications can be defined by separating them with a semicolon.

static_modifications.description: Comet parameter: set the variable modifications to overwrite in the template.The actual string MUST be in single quotes inside a string, like "'add_C_cysteine = 57.021464'". The variables are defined like in the comet params file (with 'add_XX_... = ...'). Multiple modifications can be defined by separating them with a semicolon.

label_modifications.description: Additional Comet static modifications appended only for the labelled COMETCONFIG search. Use the same syntax as static_modifications, for example "'add_K_lysine = 8.014199;add_R_arginine = 10.008269'".

visualization_parameters.title: Visualization parameters
visualization_parameters.description: Parameters for the visualization of the QC results.

figure_format.description: Output format for figures (plotly, html, or both as 'html,plotly')

output_table_type.description: Output format for the summary table

spikeins.description: Whether spike-ins were included in the analysis. If information on identified spike-in peptides is available (spikeins = true), they can be included in the summary table and the calculation of the principle component analysis (PCA).

rt_unit.description: Unit for retention time in plots ('min', 'sec').

output_column_order.description: Order of columns for the output table, separated by commas, e.g. 'filename,startTime,nr_MS1,nr_MS2'.

spikein_columns.default: MS1 feature maximum intensity,retention time,count of identified spectra,Delta_to_expected_RT
spikein_columns.description: Spike-in columns to include in the output table, separated by commas. Available columns: 'MS1 feature maximum intensity' (maximum XIC intensity observed for the spike-in peptide), 'retention time' (observed retention time at that maximum intensity), 'count of identified spectra' (number of identified spectra/PSMs matching the spike-in peptide), 'predicted retention time' (expected retention time from the spike-ins reference table), and 'Delta_to_expected_RT' (difference between observed and predicted retention time).

height_barplots.description: Height of the bar plots in pixels.

width_barplots.description: Width of the bar plots in pixels. Default = 0 means automatic width.

height_pca.description: Height of the PCA plots in pixels.

width_pca.description: Width of the PCA plots in pixels.

height_ionmaps.description: Height of the ion maps plots in inches.

width_ionmaps.description: Width of the ion maps plots in inches.

spike_ins_table.description: Spike-ins reference table as a csv file. Please refer to the [usage docs](https://mpc-bioinformatics.github.io/McQuaC/usage) for details on the required format and columns.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

macproqc_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of specific macproqc test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).
